title: Infra Playbook: GPU Fleet, Capacity, Cloud Accounts, Terraform/IaC Modules, CI/CD & Runbooks (Addendum)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
========
This addendum consolidates infra engineering best-practices for the GPU fleet and capacity planning, cloud accounts & networking, Terraform/IaC modules, CI/CD pipelines for infra, and operational runbooks. It is intended for infra engineers, SREs, and platform owners who operate Redwood’s inference fleet and related provisioning pipelines.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Audience: Infra engineers, platform SREs, private deployments team, and on-call engineers.
- Scope: Design patterns and runbooks for: GPU fleet capacity management, cloud account structure, network topology, Terraform module usage, CI/CD for infra, and common operational playbooks.

Summary of recommendations (TL;DR)
----------------------------------
- Standardize IaC around a small set of audited Terraform modules (v1.4+) for: cloud-account-bootstrap, vpc, subnet, gateway, route-tables, security-groups, gpu-node-pool, and iam-roles.
- CI/CD pipelines must gate plan & policy checks (tfsec, sentinel-like) and require manual approval for changes to production accounts.
- Capacity: target 95th-percentile utilization per-GPU <= 65% during business hours, with autoscale thresholds tuned to maintain 99.9% request throughput SLO.
- Networking: use hub-and-spoke VPCs per-environment with centralized NAT, shared services, and per-customer-private VPC peering for Private deployments.

Architecture overview
---------------------
- Logical components: control plane (management plane resources), shared services (logging, monitoring, registry), GPU worker pools (node pools), and customer/private VPCs (for Private deployments).
- Account layout: org-root -> management-account (billing, org mgmt) -> platform-account (shared infra) -> env-accounts (prod/staging/dev) -> customer-specific accounts when required.

Core networking design (summary table)
-------------------------------------
| Component | Purpose | Key config |
|---|---|---|
| Hub VPC (platform-account) | Shared services: NAT, jump hosts, ECR, monitoring endpoints | 3 AZs, centralized NAT gateways, flow logs enabled |
| Spoke VPC (env-account) | GPU workloads, autoscaling groups, node pools | Private subnets (no IGW), dedicated route tables |
| Customer VPC (private-deploy) | Isolated customer compute | VPC peering or Transit Gateway, restricted CIDR |

Terraform/IaC modules & patterns
--------------------------------
- Module set (canonical names): cloud-account-bootstrap, vpc, subnet, bastion, iam-core, iam-gpu, gpu-node-pool, autoscaler, metrics-exporter, monitoring-endpoint.
- Versioning: lock module versions in registry; every change must have a module changelog and be reviewed.

Example usage (module invocation, truncated):
```
module "gpu_node_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo.redwood.ai/infra/modules//gpu-node-pool?ref=v1.4.2"
  name   = "gpu-pool-prod-a"
  instance_type = "nvidia-h100-80gb"
  desired_count = 12
  min_count     = 6
  max_count     = 48
  subnet_ids    = module.vpc.private_subnet_ids
  tags = { team = "infra", service = "inference" }
}
```

Module inputs (recommended required fields)
- name (string)
- instance_type (string)
- min_count / desired_count / max_count (numbers as strings in this doc)
- subnet_ids (list of strings)
- enable_gpu_metrics (bool as string: "true"/"false")

CI/CD & build pipeline patterns
--------------------------------
- Repo layout: infra-modules/*, infra-accounts/*, infra-pipelines/*.
- Pipeline stages (required): lint -> fmt -> plan (with workspace per-account) -> tfsec -> module-unit-tests -> manual-approval (prod only) -> apply (with audit logging).
- Gate policy checks: enforce tag policy, disallow public IPs on private node pools, require KMS encryption for EBS & S3.

Example GitHub Actions (infra plan stage snippet):
```
name: Terraform Plan
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v2
        with:
          terraform_version: 1.4.6
      - name: Terraform Init
        run: terraform init -backend-config="bucket=${{ secrets.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}"
      - name: Terraform Plan
        run: terraform plan -out=tfplan -input=false
      - name: Upload Plan
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: tfplan
          path: tfplan
```

GPU fleet & capacity planning
-----------------------------
- Supported GPU SKUs (current): nvidia-h100-80gb, nvidia-a100-40gb, nvidia-h100-80gb-quant. Use SKU mapping file (infra/config/gpu-skus.yaml) to map model footprints to SKU.
- Capacity rules: maintain on-demand headroom of 20% across each AZ for burst; maintain reserved capacity for steady-state (committed instances) where predictable throughput is required.
- Autoscaling policies (recommended): scale-up when average queue wait > 12s for 3m; scale-down when average utilization < 30% for 10m and node tail-latency < 200ms.
- Cost controls: prefer spot/interruptible instances for non-critical background workloads; never use >30% spot for production-critical pools without fallback policy.
- SLOs (fleet level):
  - Throughput availability: 99.9% monthly (requests served without queue delay > 5s)
  - Median latency per-token: < 50ms on h100 SKU for inference-ready models
  - Provisioning time: 95th percentile scale-up time < 6 minutes (from scale signal to node ready)

Operational runbooks (common scenarios)
---------------------------------------
1) Capacity saturation (signs): sustained queue length > 200 requests or average queue waiting time > 60s.
   - Steps:
     1. Check autoscaler logs: `kubectl -n infra logs deployment/autoscaler` or cloud autoscaling console.
     2. Verify node pool quotas: `gcloud compute regions describe <region>` / AWS describe-instance-quotas.
     3. If quota limited, open fast-track quota request (link in related pages) and enable emergency burst pool: toggle `gpu_burst_pool` feature flag in infra-config.
     4. If still saturated, route low-priority workloads to production-burst account using routing policy.
     5. Post-incident: create incident in PagerDuty, tag playbook `capacity-saturation`, and schedule capacity review.

2) Node GPU OOM / driver crash
   - Steps:
     1. Identify failing node: `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector=status.phase!=Running` or cloud console GPU health metrics.
     2. Drain node, cordon to prevent scheduling: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then `kubectl cordon <node>`.
     3. Restart NVidia driver daemonset: `kubectl rollout restart ds/nvidia-driver` in infra namespace.
     4. If driver restart fails, reprovision node from template: `terraform apply -target=module.gpu_node_pool` for the node pool (use non-prod workspace first).
     5. File a bug with runtime team and include GPU diagnostics (`nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.memory --format=csv`).

3) Terraform unexpected change detected in prod
   - Steps:
     1. Revert via PR: check last apply plan artifact; if plan pending, cancel apply.
     2. Run `terraform state pull` and compare with repo.
     3. If drift is legitimate and safe, prepare patch in infra repo, run plan in staging, and promote via normal promotion flow.
     4. If not safe, restore state from latest snapshot and open incident.

Metrics and alerting (must-haves)
---------------------------------
- Fleet-level dashboards: GPU utilization heatmap by AZ, queue length by priority, scale events per hour.
- Critical alerts (pager):
  - queue_wait_time > 60s for > 5m (severity P1)
  - scale_event_failures > 3 in 10m (P1)
  - node_reboot_rate > 5% of fleet in 15m (P2)

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Fleet owner: infra-gpu-team (Primary: Aisha Patel, on-call rotation: infra-gpu-sre).
- Networking: cloud-networking-team (Primary: Daniel Kim).
- IaC & CI/CD: infra-cicd-team (Primary: Marta Gonzalez).

Change management & release process
----------------------------------
1. All infra module changes require: unit tests for modules, integration plan runs against non-prod, and documented impact in PR description.
2. Production changes require mandatory 48-hour review window for large surface-area changes (networking, IAM, gpu-pools > 10% capacity change).
3. Use feature flags for toggling new autoscaler logic; implement canary rollout (10% of nodes) then promote after 24h observation.

Appendix: quick reference (commands & links)
-------------------------------------------
- Check GPU pool sizes: `gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels:gpu-pool"`
- Terraform apply to non-prod: `TF_WORKSPACE=staging make terraform-apply`
- Emergency quota request: https://cloud-provider/quotas/request (org SSO required)
- Module registry: git@repo.redwood.ai:infra/modules

Related pages and artifacts
--------------------------

Document maintenance
--------------------
- Owner must review quarterly or after any production incident that involves GPU fleet scaling or network changes.
- Major version bump required when module contracts change; keep changelog in `infra/modules/CHANGELOG.md`.

End of document.
